title: Left-handed and left-footed playing
summary: Watkins does everything left-handed and kicks the bass drum with his left foot, which feels natural.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: I was going to ask a few more questions. Yeah, go ahead. One thing, you're left-handed of course. I guess you were always… Always was left-handed. You're right-left-handed and eat left-handed. Right-left-handed, eat…
I do everything left-handed. Left-handed. Left-handed.
I'm ashamed to say, I don't remember now, the foot on your base…
You used the left foot. I don't even know.
Yeah, I used my left foot. I should have seen that, but I don't know.
You see my snare drum sits on the right-hand side.
I knew that. But I forgot if you used your left foot, I could use your dits. No, no.
I used my left foot. Does that seem more natural?
Yeah, it does. Yeah, it does.
It seems more natural. If you had to use your right foot, could you do it, do you think?
I'd have to take about six months practice to get accustomed to it, yeah.

Because some musicians, I know they count with their left foot, like when I used to play violin, I'd count with my left foot as much as the right, I think. Uh-huh. So I thought maybe it'd be just as easy for you to use your right foot.
